quote: But I I got a renter there, so I'm not paying it there. But Oh, okay. Cool.
stewart_read: Dave explicitly disclosed he does not personally pay the $400 bill — this is not a personal bill-pain scenario, it's a landlord decision. The rep's 'Oh, okay. Cool.' treats this as a neutral aside rather than the single most important framing fact for the entire pitch: the value proposition here is rental yield / property value / tenant incentive, not personal bill relief.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that reframing mid-call would slow down an already-cooperative customer, deferring the framing shift to the closer. But there's no evidence in the transcript the rep flagged this distinction anywhere, including at button-up, so this reads as a missed capture rather than a deliberate deferral.
coaching_implication: Train the rep to explicitly name the landlord-economics angle once disclosed ('so this would really be about lowering the utility cost for a future tenant and boosting the property's value') so the framing carries into the handoff, not just the number.

quote: $16 summertime bill sounds really good with me. Yeah.
stewart_read: Dave volunteers a striking historical result (a $16 summertime bill) from his own prior solar system — strong proof-of-concept enthusiasm. However, this figure is 26 years old and tied to a different property, so its direct transferability to the rental-house pitch is weak; it's a rapport signal more than a usable financial anchor.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to acknowledge this kind of legacy-result enthusiasm as a trust-builder ('that's great to hear it worked out that well for you') without treating it as a substitute for capturing the CURRENT property's real bill — which the rep did correctly continue to pursue.

quote: It's in trust. It's my brother's trust and I'm a trustee. So
stewart_read: The property is held in a trust with Dave as trustee, not sole owner — an ownership structure the schema's verify/co-owner logic doesn't explicitly cover (that logic addresses spouses on title, not trustee/beneficiary arrangements). The rep says only 'Okay. Gotcha. Gotcha.' and moves on without confirming whether the trust or beneficiary has any decision authority over a solar install.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged trustee authority as sufficient for the sole decision-maker and correctly not slowed the call down — this is plausible given Dave speaks with full authority throughout the call.
coaching_implication: Flag as a schema gap for Kenny: does Ion's title/ownership verification need a trustee-authority check, and should the closer confirm trustee sign-off authority before finalizing a contract?

quote: Now did you take a satellite view yet and look at the house?
stewart_read: Dave is engaged enough to check the rep's homework — this is a customer leaning in, not pulling away. The rep's answer ('Yeah. I'm looking at it here... looks pretty good') is accurate but generic, and the rep is then corrected by Dave on the garage-vs-house misread at 05:15, which slightly undercuts credibility right after Dave tested it.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to slow down on satellite/roof review before stating conclusions aloud — a specific, confident answer here builds more trust than a fast one that turns out wrong.

quote: a generator that formerly was there, and I probably have enough electric capacity to push it back up to the house because everything runs through the house.
stewart_read: Dave references a former generator and existing electrical capacity considerations — adjacent to Ion's Tesla Powerwall battery offering, which isn't in the schema's cross-sell catalog yet but is directly relevant context (customer already thinking about backup power and electrical routing). The rep's response focuses only on solar placement, not on flagging this as a potential battery-interest signal for the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have reasonably treated this as pure electrical-routing detail for the design team rather than a battery-interest signal, since Dave didn't ask about backup power directly.
coaching_implication: Note in the closer handoff that Dave has existing generator/capacity infrastructure — worth probing for Powerwall/battery interest at the appointment.

quote: Do you have a program where you put a roof on too? Or
stewart_read: Dave directly asks about Ion's roofing program at the very end of the call, right after mentioning the house roof is roughly 20 years old (03:36-03:40). This is a textbook cross-sell trigger — the schema's positive example is bridging in real time and capturing roof material/urgency for the roofing team.
coaching_implication: The rep answered honestly but passively ('I don't know a ton of the details') and never captured which roof (house vs garage), material, or timeline for the roofing team — a live opportunity was named by the customer and left un-routed.

quote: I don't know, like, a ton of the details, especially for the roofs, but our, our specialist would know know all about that for you.
stewart_read: The rep correctly avoids fabricating roofing program details and redirects to the specialist — good scope discipline. But the redirect is passive; it doesn't capture the lead detail (20-year-old house roof) that would let the roofing team follow up with urgency.
coaching_implication: This is the right instinct (don't guess) executed with the wrong follow-through (no capture). Coach the rep to pair 'I'll let the specialist cover that' with a quick data-grab: 'so I can flag it for them, is it the house roof you'd want redone, or the garage?'
